definition: Dots is OpenAI's persistent agent for ongoing work. It learns your preferences and goals, runs on its own cloud computer, and connects to thousands of apps through ChatGPT, Slack, and Teams.
extendedDescription:
The idea behind Dots is simple: an agent that stays on the job after the chat ends. It keeps your goals, learns from feedback, and keeps working in the background.

As of 2026 the surface is still evolving, so exact capabilities are moving. Treat anything you read about Dots as a snapshot, not a spec sheet.

Dots shares one limit with every closed agent: it runs on OpenAI's cloud, so you cannot inspect the code or host it yourself. That control gap is what an open assistant fills.

faqs.answer: Dots is a persistent agent that keeps working after the chat ends. It is the always-on lane, not the open assistant.
faqs.question: What is OpenAI Dots?

faqs.answer: Both remember and act. The difference is control: Dots runs closed on OpenAI's cloud, while GAIA is open source and self-hostable with memory under your control.
faqs.question: How is Dots different from a full AI assistant?

howGaiaUsesIt: GAIA is the open assistant for work that spans tools and time. It connects to 50+ tools, builds graph-based memory of how you work, and runs on code you can inspect and host yourself.
metaDescription: Dots is a persistent agent on OpenAI's cloud. Learn what it covers and when an open-source assistant fits better.
metaTitle: What Is OpenAI Dots? Persistent Agent Explained
